= Ontology Alignment Specification: Cross-System Semantic Interoperability =

== Executive Summary

This specification defines protocols for aligning BITwiki's ontology with external knowledge systems. It enables semantic interoperability, data exchange, and federated querying across knowledge graphs.

'''Scope:''' Wikipedia, Wikidata, Schema.org, DBpedia, academic ontologies (FOAF, Dublin Core, SKOS).

----
== 1. Alignment Principles

=== 1.1 Semantic Equivalence

'''Definition:''' Two terms are semantically equivalent if they denote the same concept in the same context.

'''Alignment Types:'''

| Type | Symbol | Meaning | Example |
|------|--------|---------|---------|
| Exact | ≡ | Identical meaning | BITwiki:Concept ≡ SKOS:Concept |
| Close | ≈ | Similar meaning | BITwiki:Project ≈ Schema:Project |
| Related | ~ | Connected meaning | BITwiki:Agent ~ FOAF:Agent |
| Narrower | ⊂ | Subclass | BITwiki:RecursiveSystem ⊂ SystemsScience:System |
| Broader | ⊃ | Superclass | BITwiki:Knowledge ⊃ Schema:Thing |

=== 1.2 Context Preservation

Alignment must preserve:
* '''Epistemic context:''' Confidence, status, provenance
* '''Domain context:''' Subject area, application scope
* '''Temporal context:''' Version, creation date, validity period
* '''Provenance context:''' Source, author, derivation

=== 1.3 Bidirectional Mapping

'''Requirement:''' Alignments must support:
* BITwiki → External (export)
* External → BITwiki (import)
* Round-trip without information loss

----
== 2. External System Alignments

=== 2.1 Wikipedia Alignment

'''Challenge:''' Wikipedia is not a formal ontology but a category system.

'''Alignment Strategy:'''
* Map BITwiki entity types to Wikipedia categories
* Use Wikipedia article structure as template
* Align epistemic status with Wikipedia quality classes

'''Mapping Table:'''

| BITwiki | Wikipedia | Alignment |
|---------|-----------|-----------|
| Concept | Category:Concepts | ≈ |
| Project | Category:Projects | ≈ |
| Has domain | Category:Subject_area | ≈ |
| Epistemic status | Article quality class | ~ |
| Confidence | Citation density | ~ |

'''SMW Integration:'''
```mediawiki
[[Wikipedia category::Category:Systems_science]]
[[Wikipedia article::Systems_science]]
[[Wikipedia quality::FA]]
```

=== 2.2 Wikidata Alignment

'''Advantage:''' Wikidata is a formal knowledge base with properties.

'''Alignment Strategy:'''
* Map BITwiki properties to Wikidata properties
* Use Wikidata Q-items for entity linking
* Import Wikidata statements as BITwiki properties

'''Property Mapping:'''

| BITwiki Property | Wikidata Property | Alignment |
|------------------|-------------------|-----------|
| Has title | P1476 (title) | ≡ |
| Has author | P50 (author) | ≡ |
| Has creation date | P571 (inception) | ≈ |
| Has domain | P31 (instance of) | ~ |
| Has confidence | (custom) | - |

'''Entity Linking:'''
```mediawiki
[[Wikidata item::Q12345]]
[[Wikidata label::Systems science]]
```

'''Import Query:'''
```sparql
SELECT ?item ?label WHERE {
  ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q12345 .
  ?item rdfs:label ?label .
  FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en")
}
```

=== 2.3 Schema.org Alignment

'''Advantage:''' Schema.org is widely adopted for web markup.

'''Alignment Strategy:'''
* Map BITwiki types to Schema.org types
* Generate Schema.org JSON-LD from SMW
* Enable search engine discovery

'''Type Mapping:'''

| BITwiki Type | Schema.org Type | Alignment |
|--------------|-----------------|-----------|
| Concept | schema:Thing | ⊃ |
| Project | schema:Project | ≈ |
| Article | schema:Article | ≈ |
| Organization | schema:Organization | ≈ |
| Person | schema:Person | ≈ |

'''JSON-LD Generation:'''
```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Project",
  "name": "BITwiki",
  "description": "Recursive knowledge system",
  "epistemicStatus": "Established",
  "confidence": 0.88
}
```

=== 2.4 DBpedia Alignment

'''Advantage:''' DBpedia extracts structured data from Wikipedia.

'''Alignment Strategy:'''
* Use DBpedia URIs for entity linking
* Import DBpedia infobox properties
* Align categories with DBpedia ontology

'''Mapping:'''
```mediawiki
[[DBpedia resource::http://dbpedia.org/resource/Systems_science]]
[[DBpedia ontology::SystemsScience]]
```

=== 2.5 Academic Ontologies

'''FOAF (Friend of a Friend):'''
| BITwiki | FOAF | Alignment |
|---------|------|-----------|
| Agent | foaf:Agent | ≈ |
| Person | foaf:Person | ≈ |
| Has author | foaf:maker | ≈ |

'''Dublin Core:'''
| BITwiki | DC | Alignment |
|---------|-----|-----------|
| Has title | dc:title | ≡ |
| Has author | dc:creator | ≡ |
| Has creation date | dc:date | ≈ |
| Has domain | dc:subject | ~ |

'''SKOS (Simple Knowledge Organization System):'''
| BITwiki | SKOS | Alignment |
|---------|------|-----------|
| Concept | skos:Concept | ≡ |
| Has related entity | skos:related | ≈ |
| Has parent concept | skos:broader | ≈ |
| Has child concept | skos:narrower | ≈ |

----
== 3. Alignment Implementation

=== 3.1 Property Definitions

'''Alignment Properties:'''
```mediawiki
[[Has type::External identifier]]

[[Equivalent to::External property]]
[[Close match to::External property]]
[[Related to::External property]]
[[Broad match to::External property]]
[[Narrow match to::External property]]
```

=== 3.2 Import Protocol

'''Step 1: Entity Resolution'''
* Match BITwiki entities to external entities
* Create alignment properties
* Store external identifiers

'''Step 2: Property Mapping'''
* Define property transformations
* Handle value format differences
* Preserve epistemic context

'''Step 3: Data Import'''
* Fetch external data
* Transform to BITwiki format
* Set epistemic status (imported data = Hypothetical)

'''Step 4: Validation'''
* Verify alignment accuracy
* Check for information loss
* Update confidence scores

=== 3.3 Export Protocol

'''Step 1: Entity Selection'''
* Select high-confidence entities
* Filter by export criteria
* Prepare external identifiers

'''Step 2: Format Transformation'''
* Convert SMW to RDF/JSON-LD
* Map properties to external schema
* Preserve epistemic markers

'''Step 3: Data Export'''
* Generate export files
* Validate against external schema
* Publish to endpoint

'''Step 4: Synchronization'''
* Track export versions
* Handle external updates
* Maintain alignment freshness

----
== 4. Technical Implementation

=== 4.1 RDF Export

'''SMW to RDF Mapping:'''
```php
// Pseudo-code for RDF export
function smwToRdf($entity) {
    $rdf = "<rdf:Description rdf:about=\"" . $entity->getUri() . "\">\n";
    
    foreach ($entity->getProperties() as $prop => $value) {
        $mappedProp = mapToRdf($prop);
        $rdf .= "  <" . $mappedProp . ">" . $value . "</" . $mappedProp . ">\n";
    }
    
    $rdf .= "</rdf:Description>";
    return $rdf;
}
```

=== 4.2 SPARQL Endpoint

'''BITwiki SPARQL Interface:'''
```sparql
PREFIX bit: <https://bitwiki.org/ontology/>
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>

SELECT ?entity ?title ?confidence WHERE {
  ?entity bit:hasTitle ?title .
  ?entity bit:hasConfidence ?confidence .
  ?entity bit:hasWikidataItem ?wdItem .
  FILTER (?confidence > 0.8)
}
```

=== 4.3 API Integration

'''Wikidata API:'''
```python
import requests

def get_wikidata_entity(qid):
    url = f"https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Special:EntityData/{qid}.json"
    response = requests.get(url)
    return response.json()

def align_to_bitwiki(wd_entity):
    # Extract relevant properties
    # Create BITwiki entity
    # Set alignment properties
    pass
```

----
== 5. Quality Assurance

=== 5.1 Alignment Validation

'''Automated Checks:'''
* Verify external identifiers resolve
* Check property type compatibility
* Validate round-trip conversion
* Detect alignment drift

'''Manual Review:'''
* Sample alignment accuracy
* Review edge cases
* Assess semantic fidelity
* Update alignments

=== 5.2 Confidence Scoring

'''Alignment Confidence:'''
* Exact match: 1.0
* Close match: 0.8-0.9
* Related: 0.5-0.7
* Uncertain: <0.5

'''Epistemic Status:'''
* Imported alignments: Hypothetical
* Validated alignments: Emerging
* Community confirmed: Established

----
== 6. Use Cases

=== 6.1 Federated Search

Query across BITwiki and Wikidata:
```sparql
SELECT ?bitEntity ?wdEntity ?label WHERE {
  SERVICE <https://bitwiki.org/sparql> {
    ?bitEntity bit:hasDomain "Systems science" .
  }
  SERVICE <https://query.wikidata.org/sparql> {
    ?wdEntity wdt:P31 wd:Q12345 .
    ?wdEntity rdfs:label ?label .
  }
  ?bitEntity bit:hasWikidataItem ?wdEntity .
}
```

=== 6.2 Knowledge Enrichment

Import Wikidata properties to enhance BITwiki entities:
* Geographic coordinates
* Temporal data
* Relationship networks
* Multilingual labels

=== 6.3 Cross-Platform Publishing

Export BITwiki content to:
* Wikipedia (compatible articles)
* Wikidata (structured statements)
* Schema.org (web markup)
* Academic databases (RDF)

----
== 7. Maintenance

=== 7.1 Alignment Updates

'''Triggers:'''
* External ontology changes
* New entity creation
* Alignment error reports
* Scheduled reviews

'''Process:'''
# Detect external changes
# Assess impact on alignments
# Update alignment properties
# Validate changes
# Document rationale

=== 7.2 Versioning

'''Alignment Versioning:'''
* Version alignments with ontologies
* Track alignment history
* Support rollback
* Document breaking changes

----
== Conclusion

Ontology alignment enables BITwiki to participate in the broader knowledge graph ecosystem while maintaining epistemic rigor and recursive self-awareness.

'''Key Principles:'''
* Preserve epistemic context across systems
* Support bidirectional data flow
* Maintain alignment quality
* Enable federated knowledge

'''Next Steps:'''
# Deploy alignment properties
# Implement import/export pipelines
# Establish SPARQL endpoint
# Validate with external systems

=== 4.1 RDF Export

'''SMW to RDF Mapping:'''
```php
// Pseudo-code for RDF export
function smwToRdf($entity) {
    $rdf = "<rdf:Description rdf:about=\"" . $entity->getUri() . "\">\n";
    
    foreach ($entity->getProperties() as $prop => $value) {
        $mappedProp = mapToRdf($prop);
        $rdf .= "  <" . $mappedProp . ">" . $value . "</" . $mappedProp . ">\n";
    }
    
    $rdf .= "</rdf:Description>";
    return $rdf;
}
```
